stdoutProtocol.protocolDescription: handler.py requires the CLI worker subprocess's ENTIRE stdout stream to be exactly one JSON document -- not one JSON line among others, not the final JSON line, not a JSON-looking substring. Any byte written to stdout before or after the worker's own single print(json.dumps(result)) call breaks this contract and is rejected as RuntimeError('worker produced invalid non-JSON output').
stdoutProtocol.workerOwnStdoutDiscipline: worker.py's own code writes to stdout exactly once, on the success path only (print(json.dumps(result)) in main()); every error path prints to stderr. worker.py's own source is stdout-clean by construction.

confirmedRootCause.mechanism: handler.py's subprocess.run() call omits cwd=, so the worker.py subprocess runs with CWD=/srv/handler (the Serverless container's own WORKDIR) instead of /srv/worker (the directory worker.py's own script lives in and where its symlinks are created). gfpgan==1.3.8's GFPGANer.__init__ hardcodes a RELATIVE model_rootpath='gfpgan/weights' when constructing FaceRestoreHelper, and facexlib==0.3.0's load_file_from_url resolves that relative path against the process's actual CWD, not against worker.py's script directory. With CWD=/srv/handler, facexlib looks for the auxiliary detection/parsing weights at /srv/handler/gfpgan/weights/*, which do not exist (the real files/symlinks live at /srv/worker/gfpgan/weights/*), so for BOTH auxiliary weights it prints 'Downloading: "<url>" to <path>\n\n' to stdout and attempts a genuine, unauthorized runtime network download from GitHub. If that download succeeds (plausible; RunPod GPU workers commonly have outbound internet access, and executionMs=9616ms in the observed run is consistent with a brief network fetch before GPU work), inference completes normally and worker.py appends its own single JSON line at the end -- but the combined stdout (two 'Downloading:' print blocks followed by the JSON line) is no longer a single valid JSON document, so handler.py's json.loads(proc.stdout) raises JSONDecodeError, caught and reported as exactly 'worker produced invalid non-JSON output' with the worker's own exit code remaining EXIT_OK=0 (a legitimate success codepath masked purely by the stdout-protocol violation) -- precisely matching run 30702245089's evidence (job reached IN_PROGRESS, ran 9.6s, exit implicitly 0-class since handler.py's own exit-code check passed before the JSON-parse check failed).
confirmedRootCause.reproductionMethod: Empirical, two-stage, fully offline (no network call performed; simulated downloads only), through the real subprocess boundary, using the exact real, unmodified worker.py and handler.py candidate source plus the exact pinned facexlib==0.3.0 source (pip-downloaded, unmodified, loaded directly via importlib bypassing facexlib/__init__.py so only lightweight cv2/torch stubs were needed). Stage 1 called the REAL facexlib.utils.misc.load_file_from_url function directly with the real gfpgan==1.3.8 call signature (model_dir='facexlib/weights', save_dir='gfpgan/weights') from two different working directories, proving the CWD-relative lookup: from a mismatched CWD it produced a print() to stdout (354 bytes, containing the exact string 'Downloading: "https://github.com/xinntao/facexlib/releases/download/v0.1.0/detection_Resnet50_Final.pth"') and 2 download attempts; from the matching CWD it produced 0 bytes of stdout and 0 download attempts. Stage 2 ran the REAL worker.py as an actual python3 subprocess (via a reproduction-only launcher that monkeypatches only validate_weight and cuda_info, the two functions this task's own instructions explicitly authorize mocking, plus a faithful gfpgan stub whose GFPGANer.__init__ calls the same real facexlib function and whose enhance() returns the real verified 3-tuple shape with a real Pillow-encoded PNG) with cwd=/srv/handler (buggy) and cwd=/srv/worker (fixed). The buggy run produced 813 bytes of stdout (two real 'Downloading:' blocks + the worker's own valid JSON line) that failed json.loads() as a whole; the fixed run produced exactly 459 bytes of clean, single-document JSON. The real captured buggy stdout was then fed into the REAL, unmodified handler.py's real handler() function (via mock.patch.object(H.subprocess, 'run', ...), the same technique this project's own committed test_handler.py already uses) and it returned exactly {'error': 'worker produced invalid non-JSON output', 'detail': 'worker produced invalid non-JSON output'} -- the EXACT string observed in run 30702245089. The real captured fixed stdout produced ok=true, providerPostCount=0, productionRoutingAllowed=false.
confirmedRootCause.distinctFromPriorUnpackDefect: This is a different, independent defect from the previously confirmed-and-fixed GFPGANer.enhance() 2-vs-3-value unpack bug (runs 30691401701/30692613631, EXIT_INTERNAL/exit code 1). That defect was inside worker.py's own inference call; this defect is in how the Serverless handler invokes worker.py as a subprocess (a missing cwd=), interacting with gfpgan/facexlib's own relative-path weight lookup. Both are now independently confirmed and (for this one) a fix is prepared.
